scope: Cross-domain operational census of institutional legibility mechanisms reconstructed from manuscript and zoological evidence in Waves 17-19.
governing_question: What relations had to remain addressable for a physically possessed Hodgson object to become institutionally usable after movement?

mechanisms.operational_metadata: Metadata fields are selected to support downstream actions such as finding, comparing, copying, purchasing, distributing, correcting, or publishing objects.
mechanisms.semantic_addressability: Institution can identify what an object is, what it contains, or how it should be named/classified.
mechanisms.physical_addressability: Institution can locate the physical object/container and maintain a relation between description and storage/custody state.
mechanisms.relational_addressability: Institution can preserve links among object, label, drawing, list, container, provenance, copy, body part, or distribution history.
mechanisms.catalogue_labour_economy: Budgeted expert reading, travel, transcription, form production, copying, binding, transport, checking, indexing, storage, and printing used to manufacture institutional legibility.
mechanisms.counting_ontology: Counts are operation-specific; bundle, volume, textual work, specimen, body part, drawing, catalogue entry, and distribution series are non-equivalent units.

historical_metadata_regimes.institutional_context: Government of India / Asiatic Society Sanskrit manuscript survey
historical_metadata_regimes.review_loop: Government reviewed submitted notices and demanded supplementary information where location/owner and other actionability fields were insufficient.

historical_metadata_regimes.institutional_context: Hodgson specimen/drawing identity system and British Museum incorporation
historical_metadata_regimes.record_type: paired specimen labels + numbered drawings + mutable specimen/distribution lists

failure_modes.definition: Object is physically present but name/title/content identity is insufficient for institutional use.
Object is described or expected but cannot be located at the relevant processing/custody node.
examples: bird at stuffer omitted from current list

failure_modes.definition: Object survives but links to labels, drawings, lists, containers or provenance are lost or drift.
Object temporarily disappears from a list because it is at another processing stage/node.
examples: Tibetan pheasant at stuffer when bird list prepared

failure_modes.definition: Only a material part or preparation survives/is received, requiring a distinct counting unit.
examples: Ganges Pelican represented only by a head

failure_modes.definition: Physical unit boundary is incorrectly equated with intellectual/textual object boundary.
examples: continuously paginated multi-work codex treated as one work

failure_modes.definition: Record may identify object but lacks fields needed for intended downstream action.
Physical redistribution and list/catalogue state diverge until a later update reconciles them.
examples: Gray asks for bird list so later distributions can be added

cross_domain_comparison.shared_problem: Maintain enough selected relations for a distant institution to identify, locate, compare, transform, and redistribute objects after separation from their production context.
cross_domain_comparison.manuscript_specific_problem: Textual segmentation, aliases/titles, copy state, script competence, support and ownership/location.
cross_domain_comparison.zoology_specific_problem: Organism/specimen/body-part distinction, taxonomic naming, physical condition, preparation state, specimen-drawing linkage, duplicate/reference-series construction.
cross_domain_comparison.non_equivalence_rule: Use shared infrastructure variables only after preserving domain-specific object ontology and failure modes.

archive_ingestion_protocol: Identify the historical counting unit before comparing totals.
List all metadata fields actually present on the object/document.
Infer the downstream operation each field was intended to enable only with contextual evidence.
Separate semantic, physical, and relational addressability.
Record whether the item is a first record, updated list, proof, correction, receipt, distribution ledger, or later catalogue version.
Flag reconciliation/failure events rather than smoothing discrepancies.
Preserve object-list-label-container relations as explicit edges.
Use material support/paper evidence at sheet level where images or originals permit.

upload_threshold_assessment.reason: Public-source work has independently reconstructed manuscript and zoological metadata regimes, funding/labour structures, counting ontologies and failure modes. Archival material can now be read as tests of specific mechanisms rather than as broad thematic evidence.
highest_value_next_sources: correspondence correcting identity, number, location, missing or partial object state
